raw_response: {"diagnosis": "Batch 14 re-delivered about 312 transactions as duplicate txn_ids, and some of those copies store txn_ts as epoch milliseconds (e.g., 1768716104000 = 2026-01-18 06:01:44 UTC, matching the original row) instead of ISO text, which breaks the TIMESTAMP cast. Because txn_id values are contiguous (900001 to 904802, 4802 distinct), the duplicates are re-deliveries, so deduplicating on txn_id (keeping the earliest ingest) and parsing numeric timestamps as epoch milliseconds gives the correct silver data.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.65, "pre_sql": ["CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW txn_dedup AS SELECT * EXCLUDE (rn) FROM (SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY txn_id ORDER BY ingest_ts, batch_id) AS rn FROM raw_transactions) WHERE rn = 1;"], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS WITH p AS (SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CASE WHEN regexp_matches(txn_ts, '^[0-9]+$') THEN epoch_ms(CAST(txn_ts AS BIGINT)) ELSE CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) END AS txn_ts FROM txn_dedup WHERE status = 'POSTED') SELECT txn_id, customer_id, merchant_id, amount, txn_ts, CAST(txn_ts AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM p;"}}
